scientific_scope: One analytic T0M1 paired training experiment from identical 22-parameter initial states, with deterministic generated train=12, val=6 and test=6; two fits of exactly 20 complete-train updates and no real data, saved trajectories or historical checkpoints.
deliberate_design_choices: Endpoint-only assessment of the common initial model and the two frozen training endpoints. No intermediate val evaluation, checkpoint selection, val-based stopping or in-scope finite differences.
The sole objective difference is weight one on matched-support five-point signed-margin MSE. The acceptance ratio 0.95 applies to matched unstable val margin RMSE, not MSE.
Trajectory guards use pooled normalized RMSE at 3 and 8 seconds for the complete val cohort and its true stable subset, with ratio 1.05.

No extra stiffness or damping projection is applied. Existing positive parameterizations are retained; every completed update checks gradient availability, finite gradient norm, finite parameters and finite optimizer state.
The causal initializer uses five bounded Gauss-Newton iterations, memory radius one and the existing default zero prior weight. These synthetic settings do not select real-data hyperparameters.
reviewed_checks: The independent NumPy truth, seed 2026111502, fixed mixed-excitation generator, exact 24 IDs and role order are frozen before execution. Train and val require both classes, no historical loss of synchronism and dual-step truth qualification.

An unstable target ends at its first eligible five-point confirmation point, at most 300 genuine future points; a stable target supplies 300. The forecast uses true observed history once, and identical counts mask both trajectory and margin losses without entering model inputs.

Only train supplies normalization and optimizer targets. Both model endpoints are frozen before complete dual-step train, val and test scoring; the comparison gate reads val only. Test remains reporting-only.
The existing full-path numerical, COI, classification-consistency and energy-identity checks are preserved. Missing or invalid margin summaries remain null; unresolved predictions are not stable.

The wrapper enforces exact plan, review and implementation hashes, immutable one-use execution, the registered two-fit and forty-update limits, constrained Python 3.12 runtime and deterministic CUDA configuration.

budget_recomputation.explanation: Each training prediction uses seven rollouts, 2880 Torch RHS, 400 tangent RHS and five solves per train event. Evaluation covers three frozen models and two step sizes, with one full batch plus at most 24 individual isolation attempts per step. Three energy checks add one gradient and one RHS each.

prior_gradient_evidence.kind: Previously completed analytic engineering check, not an additional execution or finite-difference allowance in this plan.
prior_gradient_evidence.observed_result: Saved PASS for the shared stiffness gradient through 100 ms history inference and a 0.6 s CUDA rollout on two analytic cases; analytic 0.000488706991067253, central difference 0.0004887069919347691.
prior_gradient_evidence.boundary: This is one shared-stiffness gradient check at its declared analytic setup, not a finite-difference verification of all 22 parameters at the new training initialization.

claim_boundary: Approves the bounded paired synthetic experiment only. Its val result can support preparation of a separately registered real-data comparison; it does not authorize real-data execution, promotion, deployment or a stability certificate.
